description: Reset to genesis defaults (7 seed laws only).

seed_laws.title: Operator sovereignty
seed_laws.text: The operator is the sole source of constitutional authority. No agent, task force, supervisor, or orchestrator may create, amend, or repeal a law without operator approval. The constitution governs all agent behavior. Silence in the constitution means escalate — never assume permission. Every operator decision on an escalation is recorded as legislation (precedent, task force law, or amendment) for future runs.

seed_laws.title: Do no harm to the source
seed_laws.text: No agent may alter, fabricate, or suppress information from source documents. An agent may flag, annotate, footnote, and warn — but the source record is sacred. When source content conflicts with external evidence, both are preserved and the operator decides. No agent may resolve a factual conflict by choosing one version over another.

seed_laws.title: Know your bounds
seed_laws.text: Each agent has a fixed capability set defined in the agent registry. An agent may request another agent's service but may not perform another agent's function. An agent that detects itself reasoning outside its defined scope must stop and yield to the appropriate agent. The capability boundary is the agent's identity — crossing it is not initiative, it is malfunction.

seed_laws.title: No self-audit
seed_laws.text: No model may verify, fact-check, or audit output that was generated by the same model family. Claude-generated content is audited by GPT or local models. GPT-generated content is audited by Claude or local models. Local model output is audited by cloud models. The audit trail must show which model produced and which model verified every output segment.

seed_laws.title: Protect what is private
seed_laws.text: Sensitive content — PII, classified material, institutional secrets, content marked for redaction — must be processed exclusively by offline agents running on local hardware. No sensitive content may traverse a network, enter an API call, or leave the operator's machine. This law cannot be overridden by any subsequent legislation, precedent, amendment, or operator instruction. It outranks LAW-0 for this specific scope. A single leak is irreversible.

seed_laws.title: Remember before you act
seed_laws.text: Before executing any search, verification, or computation, an agent must check in order: (a) the constitution for governing law, (b) the precedent registry for prior rulings, (c) the verification memory for cached results, (d) the run objectives for alignment. Act on the first match found. Only when all four are silent may the agent proceed with a novel action — and that action's outcome must be recorded for future consultation.

seed_laws.title: Structure is earned, not assumed
seed_laws.text: All organizational structure below the Top Orchestrator emerges from identified work. Agents form task forces by drafting charters. Charters require constitutional approval from the Top Orchestrator, which checks against existing legislation. If the constitution is silent on the proposed pattern, the Top Orchestrator escalates to the operator. Approved charters become task force laws upon dissolution. No structure persists beyond its purpose — a task force with no remaining work must dissolve. No agent may invent work to justify its existence.

amendments.title: Verification cache subsystem rename
amendments.reason: Naming consistency with the renamed verification cache subsystem (module memory.py -> verification_cache.py, class VerificationMemory -> VerificationCache, data files verification_memory.json -> verification_cache.json and global_verification_memory.json -> verification_cache_global.json and search_cache.json -> search_cache_session.json). Frees the term 'ontology' for the future knowledge-graph subsystem (snapshot manager renamed ontology_manager.py -> snapshot_manager.py, functions *_ontology -> *_snapshot, folder ontologies/ -> snapshots/, manifest _ontology.json -> _snapshot.json). The LAW-V check_order token is applied identically in both constitution copies (config/constitution.json and the _GENESIS_CONSTITUTION template in scripts/snapshot_manager.py).
amendments.note: LAW-V immutable text is unchanged; only the machine-readable check_order token is renamed. This token is declarative metadata and is not consumed programmatically.

amendments.title: Per-agent model selection from the registry

change.per_agent_model_source: config/agent_registry.json (spec.model) is the sole source of each agent's exact model id; backend still selects the family (LAW-III cross-family audit preserved)
change.key_reader_isolation: load_api_keys reads API-key values only; any model variable in the external key file (e.g. a model = ... line in config.py located via .env_path) is ignored and can never influence model selection
change.deprecated_model_gate: at run start, each assigned model is resolved against the provider's live model list; a retired model STOPS the run unless the operator approves a replacement (never auto-swapped); approvals recorded to output/audit/model_approvals.json

amendments.reason: Make per-agent model selection real and registry-driven. Previously agent_wrapper chose the model by backend with a hardcoded default and a key-layer MODEL override, and model_tier/context_tier were dead config. Now each agent's exact model id lives in agent_registry.json, the key reader is isolated from model selection, and a live deprecated-model gate enforces current models with operator approval.
amendments.note: Backends/families unchanged (LAW-III preserved). Tiers: LEGAL_ANALYST and AMENDMENT_DRAFTER on Opus; PROCESSOR/ARCHIVIST/CITATION_RESOLVER on Sonnet; SPEECH_ACT_TAGGER/INST_FINDER/STYLE_GUARDIAN on Haiku; VERIFIER/FACT_CHECKER/PRACTICE_AUDITOR on GPT; REDACT_* on local Qwen.

amendments.title: Broad shared input-format family

change.shared_extractor: scripts/text_extract.py is the single text-extraction utility used by every document reader
change.embedding_store: now embeds every accepted format, not just PDF (fixes silent skip of non-PDF context)
change.unsupported_handling: logged warning + skip, never a silent drop

amendments.reason: Make document input a broad, consistent format family with full support. Previously each reader accepted a different, narrower set (embedding store PDF-only; corpus loader pdf/txt/md/rst/log; convention parser json/txt/md/rst/pdf; date cascade PDF-only), silently skipping the rest. A single shared extractor now gives every reader the same family.
amendments.note: Heavy libraries (pypdf, python-docx, beautifulsoup4) are imported lazily; a missing one degrades to a warning for that format rather than a crash. The Part XIX corpus-acquisition validator stays PDF-specific by design (it guards web-downloaded files, not operator-supplied inputs).

amendments.title: Per-document language detection, per-language embedding, direction-aware output

change.language_detection: scripts/language_detect.py detects each document's dominant language (offline langdetect, lazy import; 'und' when unavailable) and decides script direction from Unicode ranges (no dependency, no hardcoded language assumption)
change.per_language_embedding: embedding_store maps language -> model (English/undetected -> all-MiniLM-L6-v2; other -> paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2; extensible registry); unavailable models degrade to multilingual/English default with a warning
change.query_passage_consistency: store keeps one sub-store per model and records the embedding model per passage; a query is embedded separately by each model and scored only against that model's passages (valid same-model cosine), results merged for global top-k
change.staleness: rebuild on context filename-set change OR language->model registry change OR legacy single-model schema
change.direction_aware_output: docx_builder sets w:bidi/w:rtl/right-justification/bidi-language-tag per paragraph and per run from detected script; mixed LTR/RTL handled per run

amendments.reason: Make non-English (especially RTL) review first-class: detect language per document, embed with a language-appropriate model while keeping retrieval math valid (same-model query/passage), and render deliverables in the correct reading direction. Does NOT touch the agent layer, agent-registry models, or cross-family verification (LAW-III) — only the embedding model and document output.
amendments.note: langdetect and the multilingual model are optional/lazy: missing langdetect -> documents treated as English default (no surprise download) and script-based RTL/LTR still works; missing multilingual model -> graceful fallback with warning. English behavior is unchanged (same English model).

amendments.title: Protect cumulative learning (durable-vs-disposable firewall)

change.protected_class: the embedding store/cache; the verification cache (project tier-2 and global tier-3); discovered learnings (institution registry, citation conventions, speech-act taxonomy, search-strategy learnings, discovered APIs, document dates); the linguistic-identity and situational-awareness reference assets; the constitution AND its accumulated legislation (seed laws, amendments/DELTA ledger, precedents, task-force laws); the operator-approval governance ledger; saved snapshots; the reserved knowledge-graph/GNN ontology area
change.prohibition: no per-run cleanup, automatic reorganization, or normal pipeline operation may delete, truncate, or destructively relocate any member of the protected class; per-run isolation applies ONLY to what a run produces
change.structural_guarantee: the protected class must not live inside any per-run or auto-cleaned tree, so cleanup mechanisms are structurally incapable of reaching it
change.reset_constraint: snapshot reset/load are the sole authorized way to discard/replace learned state and only as an explicit operator action; reset is non-destructive by construction (snapshot-first, always backs up before stripping) and never deletes the GOVERNANCE HISTORY (the constitution's amendments[]/precedents/task-force laws and the operator-approval governance ledger survive reset untouched)
change.amendment_tripwire: scripts/constitution_guard.py intercepts any attempt to modify or delete an existing entry in constitution.json amendments[] or seed_laws from ANY code path (Constitution.save, reset/load/snapshot, or any agent). Such a change STOPS and requires explicit operator approval via the operator-escalation pattern; without approval it does not happen. Appending a new amendment (the normal DELTA path) is allowed. Agents cannot bypass it: they have no direct write path to constitution.json, and the guard denies any protected change that lacks an approving operator handler.
change.genesis_part: codifies genesis Part XXVII (Pipeline Hygiene Standard) section B

amendments.reason: Cumulative learning is the system's accrued value; a per-run hygiene reorganization (and the existing reset/load) must never be able to erase it. This raises the durable-vs-disposable firewall to constitutional force so that no cleanup, reset, load, or future reorganization can destroy or destructively relocate the protected class.
amendments.note: Proposed in Pass F-1, RATIFIED by the operator in Pass F-2 (operator_approved=true; in force). Enforcement: scripts/constitution_guard.py (amendment tripwire) wired into Constitution.save and snapshot load; reset_snapshot made snapshot-first and governance-preserving. See genesis Part XXVII section B.

amendments.title: Relocate the protected durable/learning class out of the disposable output tree

change.durable_root: new top-level durable/ tree holds the protected class OUTSIDE any auto-cleaned/output tree, so protection is structural (by location), not just rule-based
change.layout: durable/cache (embedding store + verification cache tier-2), durable/global (verification cache tier-3), durable/learnings (institutions, citations, speech-acts, search-strategy learnings, discovered APIs, document dates), durable/reference (linguistic identity, situational awareness), durable/governance (model_approvals, constitution_guard_log)
change.constitution_stays: config/constitution.json is NOT moved — it is governance, already firewall-protected and tripwire-guarded; moving it would add ripple without adding protection
change.single_source_of_truth: scripts/durable_paths.py defines every protected path; all writers/readers import it
change.firewall_by_location: reset_snapshot strips only durable/{cache,learnings,reference} and never iterates durable/global or durable/governance; snapshot save/load operate on the resettable durable subdirs only
change.gitignore: durable folders + .gitkeep placeholders are tracked; large caches (embedding pickle) and per-deployment runtime contents (runtime learnings, governance ledgers) are ignored

amendments.reason: Implements genesis Part XXVII section B by relocating the protected class so no per-run cleanup, reset, or reorganization can reach it by construction; completes INFRA-029 (which made the firewall constitutional) with the physical relocation.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire; not a protected modify). No agent layer, agent-registry models, or cross-family verification touched.

amendments.title: Append-only Part numbering (no gaps) and append-only amendment IDs

change.part_numbering: genesis Part numbers must form an unbroken sequence with no gaps; new Parts are appended at the end with the next sequential number — never inserted mid-sequence, never reserved/skipped to leave a gap
change.renumber_rule: a renumber to close an accidental gap is the only reason to shift Part numbers, and must update every upstream/downstream reference in lockstep (cross-references, README index/tree, verify gate, and constitution genesis_part fields), going through the amendment tripwire for any genesis_part change inside an existing amendment
change.amendment_ids: INFRA-0xx amendment IDs are append-only: never reused, inserted, or renumbered; they are independent of Part numbers and a Part renumber never moves an amendment ID
change.gap_closed: accompanies closing the prior XXII->XXIV gap: the reserved Part XXIII slot was consumed and every Part after XXII was renumbered down by one

amendments.reason: Append-only numbering keeps every existing reference stable and prevents the silent cross-reference rot that gaps and mid-sequence insertions cause. Codifies genesis Part XXVII section H.
amendments.note: Recorded in the same operator-approved change that closed the reserved-Part-XXIII gap (renumbering every Part after XXII down by one) and updated the INFRA-029/INFRA-030 genesis_part fields to the renumbered Pipeline Hygiene Standard (now Part XXVII). Those genesis_part modifications fired the constitution tripwire and were operator-approved; the INFRA-031 append is the normal allowed DELTA path.

amendments.title: Per-run output isolation (run-scoped output/runs/<run>/ folders)

change.run_folder: every run writes its artifacts into output/runs/<UTC-timestamp>__<run-id>/ (run id = 8 random hex chars); two runs never overwrite each other
change.run_context: scripts/run_context.py is the single source of truth for per-run paths (modeled on durable_paths.py); the bus, cost tracker, deliverables, reference index, audit synthesis, tier-1 search cache, run summary, and agent-layer contract-violation dumps all derive their path from the RunContext computed once at boot
change.agent_run_awareness: the orchestrator threads the RunContext into every AgentWrapper, so contract-violation dumps land in the current run's audit/contract_violations/ folder; no agent writes outside its run folder
change.collision_safe_keys: the per-document deliverable key keeps the bare filename stem when unique and qualifies as <stem>__<ext> on collision, so policy.pdf and policy.docx no longer clobber each other
change.firewall_unchanged: durable/ (INFRA-029/030) and config/constitution.json are never written into a run folder; per-run cleanup is confined to output/runs/ and is structurally incapable of reaching durable/; snapshot save/load and reset still operate only on durable/ + config
change.gitignore: output/runs/** is ignored while output/runs/.gitkeep is tracked so the folder exists on a fresh clone; the legacy output/{deliverables,audit,logs} placeholders were removed
change.gate: the verify gate runs every orchestrator/bus against a throwaway temp run folder so it stays non-mutating and never collides with a real run; REQUIRED_DIRS now lists output/runs instead of the legacy fixed subdirs

amendments.reason: Implements genesis Part XXVII section A: per-run isolation so concurrent or repeated runs never overwrite one another's artifacts, while the durable protected class stays untouched. Completes the hygiene standard's disposable-vs-durable split on the disposable side.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire; not a protected modify). recover_phase6 and bus_viewer default to the latest run with an optional --run. No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched.

amendments.title: Single canonical master with on-demand derived renders (amendments)

change.canonical_master: the amendments_payload dict (serialized verbatim as <doc_id>__amendments.json) is the single source of truth for a document's convention-review result
change.derived_renders: the .md and tracked-changes .docx are pure functions of that master (master in -> format out); they read amendment content only from the payload, so the three files cannot disagree
change.single_entry_point: scripts/amendment_render.py is the one place that writes the three amendment formats (write_amendment_deliverables); pipeline.phase_6_synthesis routes through it; the old inline md/docx writers and the dead reference_index md param were removed (pipeline._render_amendments_md is now a thin delegating wrapper)
change.documented_canvas: .docx takes the original document text as a presentation-only canvas to anchor tracked-change marks; it never supplies an amendment, and unanchored amendments still render in an 'Additional amendments' section so the .docx reflects the full master set
change.drift_guard: the entry point asserts the rendered .md reflects the master's amendment count, and a future edit that fed a render from another source would have to change this one function
change.other_outputs: cost_tracker.jsonl (append-only event master) vs cost_tracker.json (recomputed aggregate view) and audit_synthesis.md vs delta_proposals.json (two views of one summary) already follow master-and-derived and are documented as such; not changed because the two forms serve genuinely different purposes

amendments.reason: Implements genesis Part XXVII section E: one canonical master per logical output with derived on-demand renders, so human-facing formats cannot drift from the machine-readable master.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire; not a protected modify). No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched; run-scoped output paths from INFRA-032 are unchanged (same files at the same paths).

amendments.title: Retire orphaned subclass layer + tier-1 cache; add always-on redaction phase

change.retire_agents_layer: deleted the orphaned scripts/agents/ per-agent subclass package; it was imported by nothing — the pipeline drives every agent via agent_wrapper.AgentWrapper by registry name (config/agent_registry.json + config/agent_contracts.json)
change.retire_tier1_cache: removed the within-run tier-1 verification/search cache (it was opened but never written); the verification cache is now two durable tiers — project (tier-2) and global (tier-3) — unchanged otherwise (Part IX)
change.redaction_phase: added an always-on final pipeline phase (phase 9, after synthesis and before persist) over the produced deliverables; the three Qwen agents REDACT_CLERK / REDACT_AUTHORITY / REDACT_GATE are wired via AgentWrapper + their existing contracts and decide adaptively what, if anything, to redact (simplest-sufficient: only what warrants it)
change.master_render_integration: an approved + passed redaction is applied THROUGH the canonical amendments master and the md/docx are re-rendered from it (INFRA-033), so the rendered formats stay consistent
change.run_scoped_firewall: the redaction phase writes only inside the run folder and never touches durable/; every decision (REDACTION_NONE/APPLIED/NOT_APPLIED/SKIPPED) is posted to the run bus (LAW-IV)
change.safe_degrade: if the local Qwen backend is unreachable the phase posts REDACTION_SKIPPED and continues — it never crashes a keyless environment (the Qwen-required startup gate is a later pass)

amendments.reason: Removes dead wiring (orphaned subclass layer, never-written tier-1 cache) and closes the redaction gap: the REDACT_* agents were defined but never invoked. Redaction now always runs at the output boundary, screening sensitive content per LAW-IV, while preserving the canonical-master render discipline (INFRA-033) and the durable firewall (INFRA-029/030).
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire). INST_FINDER and CITATION_RESOLVER were NOT changed: they are invoked corpus-level agents whose outputs reach the bus with no downstream reader; deleting an agent needs operator approval and was flagged, not done. No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched.

amendments.title: Qwen-required startup gate with per-run operator override + GPU soft reminder

change.hard_gate: at run start (in pipeline.main boot, alongside the deprecated-model gate) the pipeline confirms the local Qwen redaction backend is reachable/configured BEFORE any agent runs; if not, the run REFUSES to start
change.per_run_override: --no-redaction-override lets the operator declare THIS run non-sensitive and proceed with no redaction; in interactive mode it requires an explicit yes/no confirmation; the waiver is per-run only, never a persistent setting
change.governance_logging: each waiver is appended to the governance ledger durable/governance/redaction_waivers.jsonl (timestamp + run id + reason), the same protected location as model approvals and the constitution-guard log (survives reset, never deleted)
change.honest_scope: the pre-run check verifies only that torch+transformers are importable and a qwen_local model id is configured (cheap, no model load, no paid call); actual model load/download + GPU placement are verified at first redaction call, where the phase degrades safely if load fails
change.gpu_soft_reminder: if Qwen is reachable but no GPU is detected, the gate prints a 'redaction slow on CPU' warning only — it never blocks and is never recorded
change.phase_cross_ref: when overridden, the always-on redaction phase (INFRA-034) still runs structurally but performs no redaction and records REDACTION_SKIPPED (operator_waived) on the run bus, consistent with its safe-degrade behavior

amendments.reason: Redaction is the always-on final pass (INFRA-034) and runs on the local Qwen backend; without Qwen there is no privacy screening at the output boundary (LAW-IV). The gate refuses to silently ship unredacted deliverables, while giving the operator a conscious, logged, per-run escape hatch for runs they declare non-sensitive.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire). GPU is a soft reminder only. The Qwen-required startup gate verifies configuration pre-run; reachability of the actual model is confirmed at first use. No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched.

amendments.title: Prompt caching on both cloud paths (Claude explicit, GPT structure-and-log)

change.stable_prefix_first: every agent prompt is assembled stable-prefix-first: a STABLE prefix (agent identity + DO/DO-NOT + directives + output contract + constitution + compiled conventions, identical across an agent's calls within a run) followed by a DYNAMIC suffix (objectives, precedents, retrieved passages, recent bus, work payload). agent_wrapper.build_prompt returns (stable_prefix, dynamic_suffix); bus_reader.ContextPackage classifies CONSTITUTION + CONVENTION_REGISTRY as stable, everything else dynamic. Same information as before, reordered stable-first
change.claude_explicit: call_claude marks the end of the stable prefix with cache_control {type: ephemeral} (5-minute TTL — a run fires its agent calls within minutes, so the 5-min window covers reuse without the 2x one-hour write premium); cache reads bill 0.1x, 5-min writes 1.25x; the prefix is an exact match with no dynamic content
change.gpt_structure_and_log: OpenAI caches automatically, so call_gpt adds NO cache_control; it only concatenates the prompt stable-prefix-first so OpenAI's automatic prefix cache catches, then verifies it via the logged cached_tokens field
change.cache_cost_tracking: the cost tracker records and logs each provider's cache fields per call (Anthropic cache_creation_input_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens; OpenAI prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens) into cost_tracker.jsonl + the aggregate snapshot, defaulting to 0 when absent (never crash); cost is computed cache-aware (Claude read 0.1x / write 1.25x, OpenAI cached 0.5x). A silent provider-side cache loss shows the cached count dropping to zero rather than hidden
change.no_dynamic_in_prefix_rule: no dynamic content (timestamp, run id, per-call text, retrieved passages, bus) may enter the stable prefix; doing so changes the prefix per call and drops the hit rate to near zero. Caching applies only above each model's minimum cacheable prefix size; small-prompt agents that do not meet it simply do not cache, and nothing is padded
change.unchanged: purely a cost optimization on the call paths: cross-family verification (LAW-III), the Qwen redactors, the bus, contracts, and all agent logic are unchanged; the model sees the same effective prompt information for every agent, reordered stable-first

amendments.reason: Input tokens dominate cost (the corpus-level agents read the full context digest, and per-doc agents repeat the constitution + conventions every call). Reusing a cached stable prefix across a run's many calls cuts input cost sharply; logging the cache fields makes the win measurable and a silent cache loss visible.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire). TTL choice: 5-minute ephemeral. No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched.
